content.user_title: Explore Database Schemas in DBX Studio
content.value_statement: Database teams often need a quick view of tables, relationships, and data quality before analysis. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured DBX Studio profiling workflow.
actual_capabilities: Lists database tables by starting with read_schema.
Describes selected tables with column names, data types, and table statistics.
Profiles row counts, sample rows, null rates, and value distributions.
Identifies likely table relationships from foreign key naming patterns.
Provides SQL examples for counts, null rates, distinct values, and date ranges.
Formats findings as tables, relationships, quality flags, and suggested next queries.
limitations: Requires DBX Studio database tools such as read_schema, describe_table, get_table_stats, and get_table_data.
Does not execute migrations, change data, or create database objects.
Relationship discovery is heuristic when explicit foreign keys are unavailable.
Large tables may need sampling or limits to avoid expensive profiling queries.

use_cases.title: Map a New Database
use_cases.description: Review tables, row counts, columns, and likely relationships before starting analysis.

use_cases.title: Prepare Data Quality Review
use_cases.description: Profile completeness, null rates, and value distributions to find columns that need cleanup.

use_cases.title: Plan Safe Follow-up Queries
use_cases.description: Summarize explored tables and suggest next questions without modifying data.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Public Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the data exploration workflow on schema public. List tables, describe the main tables, and summarize row counts and relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Profile One Table
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore the orders table. Report columns, data types, row count, sample fields, null rates, and useful next questions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Related Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore users, orders, and payments. Identify likely join keys, data quality flags, and analysis-ready relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Exploration Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a structured database exploration report for schema public. Include table coverage, quality scoring, relationship assumptions, and prioritized follow-up queries.

output_examples.output: A table inventory with row counts, important columns, likely relationships, quality flags, and suggested next queries.

output_examples.input: Profile the customers table for completeness.
output_examples.output: A completeness summary showing populated fields, high-null columns, sample-based distribution notes, and cleanup priorities.

output_examples.input: Find how orders connect to users.
output_examples.output: A relationship note describing likely user keys, confidence level, supporting columns, and validation queries to run next.

best_practices: Start with schema discovery before profiling individual tables.
Use limits or samples when tables are large.
Label inferred relationships separately from confirmed foreign keys.
anti_patterns: Running broad profiling on every table without asking which tables matter.
Treating naming patterns as confirmed relationships without validation.
Sharing sensitive sample rows when aggregate summaries would answer the question.

faq.question: What tools does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects DBX Studio tools for schema reads, table descriptions, table statistics, and sample data.

faq.question: Can it change my database?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow is exploratory and read oriented.

faq.question: Does it detect data quality issues?
faq.answer: It guides checks for row counts, null rates, completeness scores, value distributions, and date ranges.

faq.question: How does it find relationships?
faq.answer: It looks for explicit metadata when available and common key patterns such as matching identifier columns.

faq.question: Can it work with large datasets?
faq.answer: Yes, but large tables should use limits, samples, or targeted profiling to control query cost.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
